title: Path traversal in OnReadFile via attacker-controlled fileName HTTP field
description: kSnHttpServer_OnReadFile reads the 'fileName' parameter from the HTTP request and passes it directly to kPath_Combine with kSN_HTTP_SERVER_CGI_ROOT_PATH, then opens the resulting localPath for reading and streams its contents to the response. There is no canonicalization, no rejection of '..' segments, no absolute-path rejection, and no root-jail enforcement. An unauthenticated network attacker can craft fileName values like '../../../../etc/passwd' to exfiltrate arbitrary files readable by the sensor process.

title: Path traversal in OnWriteFile via attacker-controlled file name in multipart upload
description: kSnHttpServer_OnWriteFile takes the file-name component of a multipart upload field ('data') via kSnHttpReqParser_FieldFileName and joins it with kSN_HTTP_SERVER_CGI_ROOT_PATH using kPath_Combine, then calls kFile_Save with the attacker-supplied filename and uploaded data. No canonicalization or root-jail check is performed, so '..' segments or absolute paths allow an unauthenticated network attacker to overwrite arbitrary files writable by the sensor process - including configuration files, scripts, or executables that lead to full code execution.

title: Firmware upgrade validation can be bypassed via attacker-supplied skipValidation HTTP parameter
description: kSnHttpServer_OnStartUpgrade parses a 'skipValidation' parameter from the upgrade HTTP request and forwards it directly to kSnUpgrade_StartUpgrade which calls kUpgrader_SkipValidation. With skipValidation=1, kUpgrader_Run unconditionally skips kUpgrader_RunValidation and kUpgrader_CheckArchiveCompatibility (kUpgrader.cpp:220), allowing an unauthenticated network attacker to install an arbitrary firmware image without any compatibility or integrity checks.

title: No cryptographic signature verification of firmware upgrade packages
description: kUpgrader_Run performs only compatibility/validation script checks on the upgrade archive (kFS_UPGRADER_VALIDATION_FILE plus kUpgrader_CheckArchiveCompatibility), and both checks are skippable via obj->skipValidation. The function never verifies a digital signature, HMAC, or trusted hash of the firmware contents - so any archive whose internal validation file says 'ok' (or any archive whatsoever when skipValidation is set) is accepted and installed. Combined with the unauthenticated upgrade endpoint, this allows a network attacker to permanently compromise the device with hostile firmware.

title: Blowfish encryption uses ECB mode regardless of configured cipher mode
description: xkBlowfishCipher_VEncrypt iterates over the padded plaintext in xkBLOWFISH_CIPHER_BLOCK_SIZE chunks and encrypts each block independently with xkBlowfishCipher_EncryptBlock, with no chaining or IV. The kCipher mode field is ignored. This is textbook ECB mode - identical plaintext blocks yield identical ciphertext blocks, leaking structural information about anything encrypted with this primitive (including license payloads in kGocLicense which uses cipher mode kCIPHER_CIPHER_NULL). Blowfish itself is also deprecated for new use because of its 64-bit block size (Sweet32).
